items.prompt: Binary search requires the search space to be?
choices: Ordered so a midpoint test discards half
items.whyRight: The invariant depends on sorted order (or a monotonic predicate).

items.prompt: Classic binary search time on an array is?
items.whyRight: Each step halves the remaining range.
whyWrong: Linear scan is the fallback without order.
Constant time would be direct indexing of the answer.

choices: Where the answer must still lie if it exists
That mid is always the answer
items.whyRight: You maintain a range that still contains any feasible answer.
whyWrong: left>right is the termination condition, not the ongoing invariant.

items.prompt: Binary search on answer (“minimize feasible X”) needs?
choices: A monotonic predicate: if X works, larger/smaller also works as defined
items.whyRight: Monotonicity lets you discard half the candidate Xs.
whyWrong: Random sampling does not certify optima.

items.prompt: Off-by-one bugs in binary search usually come from?
choices: Updating left/right without preserving the invariant
items.whyRight: Mishandled mid exclusion duplicates or skips the answer.

items.prompt: Why is binary search a poor fit on a singly linked list?
choices: Finding the midpoint costs linear time per probe
items.whyRight: Without random access, each mid walk kills the log n benefit.
whyWrong: Sorted lists still lack O(1) mid.
Comparisons work fine; access does not.
